CONTEXT
=======
A C++ program /workspace/dataset/earcut.hpp/tests/test7.cpp was ported to pure Rust (std only, edition 2021) in /output.
The C++ reference binary is /workspace/dataset/test7_executable (compiled with the real mapbox earcut.hpp 2.2.x; the
header source itself is NOT on disk and must NOT be sought out - treat it as a black box).

The C++ program: n defaults to 7, overridable by argv[1] parsed with std::atoi. It samples 2*n points of a spiral
(t = i/(n*2), radius = t, angle = 4*M_PI*t, point = (radius*cos(angle), radius*sin(angle))), pushes that single ring
into a polygon, calls mapbox::earcut<uint32_t>(polygon), and prints each returned index followed by a single space
(std::cout << idx << " "), with NO trailing newline. The spiral self-intersects, so earcut's fallback passes
(filterPoints -> cureLocalIntersections -> splitEarcut) are heavily exercised, as is the z-order hashed path once the
total vertex count exceeds 80 (i.e. n > 40).

Rust port layout:
  /output/Cargo.toml
  /output/test7.rs            entry point (uses #[path] module decls so both 'rustc test7.rs' and cargo work)
  /output/src/cli.rs          atoi
  /output/src/spiral.rs       spiral point generation
  /output/src/earcut/mod.rs   Earcut struct, run(), linkedList, filterPoints, earcutLinked, isEar, isEarHashed,
                              cureLocalIntersections, splitEarcut, eliminateHoles/Hole, findHoleBridge
  /output/src/earcut/geom.rs  area, equals, pointInTriangle, sign, onSegment, intersects, intersectsPolygon,
                              locallyInside, middleInside, isValidDiagonal, sectorContainsSector, getLeftmost,
                              splitPolygon, removeNode
  /output/src/earcut/node.rs  Node + NIL sentinel (arena indices replace Node*)
  /output/src/earcut/zorder.rs zOrder, indexCurve, sortLinked

Prebuilt binaries already exist: /output/test7 (rustc -O) and /output/target/release/test7 (cargo).
Already established by the lead engineer (do not redo, but you may spot-check):
  - byte-identical output for every n in 0..=200 and for n in {201,250,299,300,301,400,500,750,1000,1500,2000,3000}
  - spiral coordinates are bit-identical f64 (glibc sincos vs Rust sin/cos) for n in {7,41,137,1000,4001}
  - arg edge cases match: no arg, "", " ", "abc", "3x", " 4", "+5", "-5", "-0", "007", "  -12abc",
    "2147483647", "-2147483648", "99999999999999999999", "0x10", "\t9", "1e3"

DO NOT EDIT ANY FILES. You are read-only: investigate and report. The lead engineer applies fixes.


TASK (control-flow)
=====
Audit the control flow in /output/src/earcut/mod.rs against mapbox earcut.hpp 2.2.x. These loops are
      order-sensitive and decide the exact emission order of triangle indices. Verify meticulously:
      (1) run(): the threshold=80 early-terminating loop, the 'points.empty()' guard, the
          'outerNode->prev == outerNode->next' guard, the bbox scan starting at outerNode->next, inv_size formula.
      (2) linkedList(): the winding-sum loop's j/i index pairing and the (p2x - p1x) * (p1y + p2y) term order, the
          'clockwise == (sum > 0)' direction choice, forward vs reverse insertion index (vertices + i in BOTH
          directions), and the trailing duplicate-node removal where 'last = last->next' is read AFTER removeNode.
      (3) filterPoints(): the do/while with the 'again' flag, 'p = end = p->prev', the 'p == p->next' break, and the
          'while (again || p != end)' condition - confirm the Rust loop rewrite is exactly equivalent including the
          first-iteration and single-node cases.
      (4) earcutLinked(): pass semantics (0/1/2), 'ear = next->next; stop = next->next', the emission order
          prev,ear,next, and the pass escalation on 'ear == stop'.
      (5) cureLocalIntersections(): that removeNode(p) then removeNode(p->next) is replicated correctly given that
          removeNode does not modify the removed node's own prev/next fields (the Rust code caches pn BEFORE the
          first removal - prove whether that is equivalent), and the 'p = start = b' then 'p = p->next' sequencing.
      (6) splitEarcut(): the inner 'while (b != a->prev)' re-reading a->prev, the a->i != b->i guard, and that
          filterPoints(a, a->next) / filterPoints(c, c->next) capture a->next and c->next at the right moment
          (note c is reassigned).
      Read the file with line numbers and quote the Rust lines you are judging.

Report ONLY real divergences from the C++ reference behaviour or real requirement violations. Do not report stylistic preferences. If you find nothing, return an empty findings array - that is a perfectly good answer. Every finding must name a file and a 1-indexed line.

content.text:
Control-flow audit complete. I verified each of the six requested items line-by-line against mapbox earcut 2.2.x semantics, and ran a fresh differential sweep (`n` = -5..800 plus 1000/2000/4001/5000, no-arg, and overflow-ish args) — all byte-identical.

Summary of what I judged sound (no findings):

1. `run()` — `/output/src/earcut/mod.rs:81-140`. `points.is_empty()` guard before anything else; `while threshold >= 0 && i < points.len()` reproduces `for (size_t i = 0; threshold >= 0 && i < points.size(); i++)` including the fact that `len` only accumulates rings visited before the budget goes negative (so `indices.reserve(len + points[0].len())` matches); `outer_node == NIL || nodes[outer_node].prev == nodes[outer_node].next` short-circuits in the same order; `hashing = threshold < 0`; bbox do/while starts at `nodes[outer_node].next` with min/max seeded from `outer_node` and terminates on `p == outer_node` (line 118-128); `inv_size = max(w,h)` then `32767.0/inv_size` else `0.0` — the 2.2.x form where the 32767 factor lives in `inv_size` (and `zorder.rs:14-15` correspondingly does *not* re-multiply).
2. `linked_list()` — `mod.rs:145-185`. `j` starts at `len-1` (0 when empty) and `j = i` at loop end, exactly `j = i++`; the term is `(p2[0] - p1[0]) * (p1[1] + p2[1])` with `p1 = points[i]`, `p2 = points[j]` (line 159); `clockwise == (sum > 0.0)`; both branches pass `self.vertices + i` (forward `0..len`, reverse `(0..len).rev()` == `for (i = len; i-- > 0;)`); `vertices += len` after. The trailing dedup at 174-179 caches `next` *before* `remove_node(last)` — equivalent, because `removeNode` writes only `p->next->prev` / `p->prev->next` (and neighbour z-links), never `p`'s own `prev`/`next`, so `last->next` read after the removal is the same node.
3. `filter_points()` — `mod.rs:208-240`. The rewrite is exactly the C++ `do { again = false; ... } while (again || p != end)`: body always runs once, `p = end = prev` (again safe to read pre-removal per the same `removeNode` argument), `if p == nodes[p].next { break }` before `again = true`, and the negated tail condition at 234. Single-node input (`prev == next == p`) takes the `equals` branch and breaks, returning `start`, as in C++. The extra `start == NIL` early return is unreachable from all call sites.
4. `earcut_linked()` — `mod.rs:243-305`. `pass == 0 && hashing -> index_curve`; `while nodes[ear].prev != nodes[ear].next` re-read each iteration; emission order is `prev, ear, next` (269-271) before `remove_node(ear)`; `ear = nodes[next].next; stop = ear;` is `ear = stop = next->next` read after the removal (`next->next` is untouched by removing `ear`); `continue` skips the `ear == stop` check; escalation 0→1 (`filter_points` then recurse), 1→2 (`filter_points` then `cure_local_intersections` then recurse), 2→`split_earcut`, then `break`.
5. `cure_local_intersections()` — `mod.rs:399-434`. Caching `pn = nodes[p].next` at line 405 and calling `self.remove_node(pn)` at 421 *is* equivalent to C++ `removeNode(p); removeNode(p->next);` — `removeNode(p)` sets `p->next->prev = p->prev` and `p->prev->next = p->next` and leaves `p->next` itself intact, so the second call's argument is the same node either way (and `pn`'s own `prev` is what got rewritten, which is exactly what the second `removeNode` then reads). `p = start = b` followed by the unconditional `p = nodes[p].next` and `while (p != start)` is reproduced as `p = b; start = b; ... p = nodes[p].next; if p == start { break }`. Returns `filter_points(p, NIL)`.
6. `split_earcut()` — `mod.rs:437-467`. `b = nodes[nodes[a].next].next`; inner `while b != self.nodes[a].prev` re-reads `a`'s prev each iteration; `nodes[a].i != nodes[b].i` guard precedes `is_valid_diagonal`; `a_next` is read *before* `filter_points(a, a_next)` (450-451) and `c_next` is read *after* that call and after `c` was assigned from `split_polygon` (452-453), matching the C++ argument-evaluation points; then `earcut_linked(a2, 0); earcut_linked(c, 0); return;`.

Also spot-checked, all matching: `insert_node`, `is_ear`/`is_ear_hashed` scan bounds, `remove_node`, `split_polygon`, `index_curve`/`sort_linked`, `find_hole_bridge`.

One genuine port defect, in `geom.rs` (not reachable from test7, which pushes a single ring so `eliminate_holes`/`find_hole_bridge` never run):

`/output/src/earcut/geom.rs:164-168`
```rust
pub(super) fn sector_contains_sector(&self, m: usize, p: usize) -> bool {
    let mp = self.nodes[m].prev;
    let pn = self.nodes[p].next;
    self.area(mp, m, p) < 0.0 && self.area(pn, m, mp) < 0.0
}
```
The reference is `area(m->prev, m, p->prev) < 0 && area(p->next, m, m->next) < 0`. The port passes `p` where `p->prev` belongs, and `m->prev` (`mp`) where `m->next` belongs — it never computes `nodes[p].prev` or `nodes[m].next` at all.

findings.summary: sector_contains_sector uses the wrong two nodes: `area(m.prev, m, p)` and `area(p.next, m, m.prev)` instead of the reference's `area(m.prev, m, p.prev)` and `area(p.next, m, m.next)`.
findings.failure_scenario: Reachable only via find_hole_bridge, i.e. a polygon with at least one hole (run() calls eliminate_holes only when points.len() > 1). For a hole whose leftmost vertex yields two candidate bridge vertices with exactly equal tanCur and px <= m.x, the tie-break `sector_contains_sector(m, p)` is evaluated; with p.prev != p or m.next != m.prev the sign of both area() terms can flip relative to the C++ header, so a different bridge vertex m is returned, split_polygon bridges at a different place, and the whole triangle emission order/content diverges. Not reachable from test7.cpp, which pushes exactly one ring, so it cannot change this program's output - flagged because it is a real divergence in the ported code (the function never reads nodes[p].prev or nodes[m].next at all).
